discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed in 7ed2ef001 — this was a real gap. `apply_session_mode` runs on the `session/new` reply, but it only acts through the `session.modes` branch, so an agent that advertises mode as a config option came back in the agent default while goose still reported the previously selected mode. `apply_session_config_options` doesn't cover it either: that replays the *statically configured* options, not a mode the user selected at runtime via `/mode`.

`reapply_mode_config_option()` now re-sends the current goose mode after the swap, gated on `session_has_config_option(Mode)` so the `session.modes` path isn't double-applied.

One deliberate departure from your wording, which said to reapply "before returning success." I made it best-effort — warn, don't fail. By the time it runs, the session swap has already happened and the context genuinely is cleared. Returning `Err` would make `/clear` report failure, and per this PR's own design the caller then *preserves the token counters* — so the meter would show a full window that no longer exists. That's a worse lie than the one this PR set out to fix, and it isn't recoverable by retrying. A wrong mode is recoverable with `/mode`.

Test: `reset_context_reapplies_mode_to_a_config_option_agent`, plus an assertion on the existing reset test that an agent *without* a mode config option isn't sent a spurious one.

Fixed in eb9392e23 — the advice was self-defeating for exactly the two providers that need it most.

Reworded rather than adding a `can_reset_context()` predicate, which was my first instinct. Reset support is only truly knowable by attempting the reset, so a separate flag would be a second source of truth that can drift from what `reset_context()` actually does — the same class of problem the derived default was added to prevent. A provider could advertise `true` and still fail, and the message would lie again.

Instead the message defers to `/clear`'s own report, which already distinguishes the two cases: it either clears the agent-side conversation or says the provider still holds it. The escalation path is now self-revealing:

> Compaction is not supported with '{provider}' because it manages its own conversation context. Try /clear, which starts the agent's conversation over for providers that can reset it; if it reports that the previous conversation is still held, start a new session instead.

The `/compact` entry in `goose-cli-commands.md` carried the same unqualified "use `/clear` instead" and is updated to match.

Addressed in ce4e1ddd6. The retry is now additionally gated on `last_assistant_text.is_empty()`.

That buffer is cleared per turn, right after the provider stream is created, and only accumulates assistant text that has been yielded to the client in the no-tools path — so a non-empty value means visible content has already streamed. A transient error arriving after that point surfaces to the user instead of retrying, avoiding the duplicate/incoherent answer.

Covered by `test_no_retry_after_visible_content_streamed`, which drives a provider that streams a text chunk and then fails mid-stream, asserting: 0 retry notifications, exactly 1 call, the partial text is visible, and the error surfaces rather than retrying silently.

Good point, and agreed the text-only guard was insufficient — fixed in 13e7999a2. The retry guard now also checks `surfaced_thinking_in_turn`, which is already tracked per turn and set whenever a `Thinking`/`RedactedThinking` chunk is yielded to the client. So a mid-stream transient failure after reasoning surfaces rather than resending. Covered by `test_no_retry_after_streamed_reasoning` (a provider that streams a `Thinking` chunk then fails: asserts 0 retries, exactly 1 call, and the error surfaces).

Fair point — rather than keep adding per-type guards, I replaced them with a single `visible_content_streamed` flag in 651cca1f7. It's set whenever any visible assistant content is yielded to the client (`AgentEvent::Message(filtered_response)`), so it covers text, reasoning, images, and any future content type without further special-casing. The retry guard now reads `no_tools_called && !visible_content_streamed && !is_token_cancelled`. Covered by `test_no_retry_after_streamed_image` (a provider that streams an image then fails: 0 retries, 1 call, error surfaces). The existing text/reasoning tests still pass too.

Good catch — fixed in 31869ba. The fallback branch now sets `last_assistant_text = EMPTY_TURN_MESSAGE` before yielding, so `emit_stop_hook_blocking`/`emit_stop_hook` receive the actual final text and the trace output is preserved. This matches the existing `MAX_TURNS_MESSAGE` path.

Good catch — and this was the third time the hoisted guard shadowed an arm below it (steer, and now final-output; goal/grind were next). Rather than add another predicate, I restructured in 30b2ef1: the empty-message cleanup stays above the `match final_output` (it must run unconditionally), but the retry/fallback decision moved into a `None if empty_response =>` arm. Match ordering now handles prioritization — `Some(None)` final-output nudge, recovery-compact, pending-steer, and goal/grind all win ahead of it, so the empty-turn fallback fires only when nothing else claims the turn. Added `test_empty_turn_with_final_output_tool_nudges` (a final-output recipe that stops without calling the tool must get the mandatory nudge, not the empty-response fallback); verified it fails without the fix. Net simpler than the guard-per-branch approach.

Fixed in 263a9dc. Good catch — this was a latent issue in `RetryManager` that my restructure exposed: it pushed the "Maximum retry attempts exceeded" message directly onto `conversation`, but the agent only yields/persists `messages_to_add`, so on `MaxAttemptsReached` the message was never shown *or* saved. With `messages_to_add` cleared for an empty turn, the recipe stopped silently.

Rather than special-case it, I removed the hidden `conversation` mutation entirely: `RetryResult::MaxAttemptsReached` now **carries** the failure `Message`, and the agent routes it through the same `messages_to_add` yield + persist path as every other completion branch. So the failure is both surfaced to the user and saved to the session, whether the empty-turn cleanup ran or not.

Added `test_recipe_max_retries_surfaces_failure` (failing success check + `max_retries: 1` over empty turns) asserting the "Maximum retry attempts" message is both yielded and persisted; verified it fails against the old silent-stop behavior.

**Fixed in 571b0bb53c.** Replaced the last-character heuristic with a full delimiter-balance scan that tracks string state, nesting depth, and escape sequences. `looks_truncated` now returns `true` for any unclosed string, unmatched closer, or leftover openers — so `{"items":[1,2]` and `{"patch":{"path":"x"}` are correctly detected as truncated and blocked from the `safely_parse_json` repair fallback.
